rationale: bugs_open/238's detection half (PBP-040) has been code-complete and in the running binary since v1.0.1291, and is ARMED NOWHERE. Measured 2026-08-19/20, read-only: ZERO active agent_definitions rows carry `record_dead_url_controls` or `refuse_dead_url_controls`, and ZERO `dead_url_control` work items exist in all platform history. The register still described the Go half as 'INERT until the chassis image rolls' and the config half as HELD — the first clause has been stale since 2026-08-12 (§9.1 of the bug file said so; the register was never corrected), and the hold condition it was waiting on has been satisfiable for eight days. So the only thing between this estate and its own detection for this class was a config key nobody set, and a status line that made not setting it look correct. This submission arms the RECORD-ONLY half on the re-render path and declares the key on the action that reads it. It deliberately does NOT arm the refusal (380_*_HOLD.sql): the refusal can block a rebuild of a page whose data is still damaged, so per the owner's decision this session it is sequenced AFTER the known damaged set is remediated or parked (migrations 498/499, separate submission). Arming record-only first is the half with no blocking behaviour at all — it files a work item and changes no disposition — and it is the only detection this class has on the re-render path, which is also the repair vehicle. Two live findings drove the shape. (1) The key was UNDECLARED on RerenderPageSectionsInputSpec, exactly as `refuse_dead_url_controls` was undeclared on RenderComponentInputSpec until 2026-08-19: neither flag reaches its action through the input extractor (both are read via a helper taking `config`), so no literal `config["..."]` appears in either function body and the 2026-08-18 declaration census could not see them. Arming an undeclared key on THIS spec is safe — it is CheckConfig, not StrictConfig, read at the deciding arm in platform/validation/workflow.go:185-195 before touching anything — but it makes a live working setting read as 'keys this action does not read, silently ignored at execution', whose stated remedy is to DELETE the key. A report that tells the next reader to disarm a working guard is that report's one dishonesty surface. The same omission on a StrictConfig spec took the fleet's page-publishing path down for 33 minutes on 2026-08-19 (WRONG_CALLS, migration 494), which is why this was checked rather than assumed. (2) The step path is NOT 380's. page-content-writer nests its render steps inside a `process_sections_loop` sub_workflow; page-rerender does not — read live 2026-08-20, all ten of its steps sit at {workflow,steps,<name>} and the one carrying this action is `rerender_sections`. Copying 380's nested path would have found nothing and read as 'no such step'. Counted in the unit of the change (WRONG_CALLS 2026-08-11, the AGENTS-vs-STEPS error made in this bug's own slice B): a text match returns three agent types mentioning the action string, a jsonb traversal of $.**.steps for action='rerender_page_sections' returns exactly ONE step fleet-wide, and the verify block re-derives that count at apply time and demands every such step carries the flag, so a second one appearing later fails the file loudly instead of shipping partial coverage under a complete label.

plan.summary: Arm bugs_open/238's record-only dead-URL emit on page-rerender's rerender_sections step (migration 497), and declare the config key on the action that reads it (Go, already committed at bb6600e48 so it rides the next build). The refusal half (380_*_HOLD) is deliberately NOT armed here — it is gated on the damaged set being drained first. Record-only refuses nothing and blocks no page; it turns a class that has been undetectable on this path into a queryable work item.

edits.rationale: Declare record_dead_url_controls on the action that has read it since the guard shipped. Not a behaviour change: it makes the unknown-config-key report honest about a key migration 497 arms. Mirrors the 2026-08-19 declaration of refuse_dead_url_controls on RenderComponentInputSpec, including its reasoning about ConfigKeys-vs-Optional and the RFC_022 counter. Committed at bb6600e48 (before this submission existed, hence no trailer on it — the trailer gate correctly refuses a non-UUID join key).

- ConfigKeys: []string{"strip_literal_markdown"},
+ ConfigKeys: []string{"strip_literal_markdown", "record_dead_url_controls"},
plus a comment block recording: read via recordDeadURLControls(config) so a function-body grep cannot see it; the cost of the omission is the report's honesty, not a broken render; CheckConfig not StrictConfig verified at the deciding arm because the same mistake on a StrictConfig spec cost 33 minutes of fleet page-publishing on 2026-08-19; no RFC_022 budget impact and why.

edits.rationale: Pins BOTH dead-URL flags as recognised by their own actions, so the next declaration census cannot silently lose one again. Refuses to pass vacuously: it fails if the action is not opted into unknown-key detection at all, so a spec that stopped checking cannot read as a spec that declares. MUTATION PROVED: removing record_dead_url_controls from ConfigKeys fails it with the exact report text the arming would have produced ('rerender_page_sections arms "record_dead_url_controls", but the action reports it as unrecognised'); restored and re-run green.
edits.sketch: table over {rerender_page_sections, deadURLRecordConfigKey} and {render_component, deadURLGuardConfigKey}; datahelpers.UnknownConfigKeys(action, {key: true}); t.Fatalf if !checked (vacuous-pass guard), t.Errorf if len(unknown) != 0.

edits.rationale: The arming itself. Not a _HOLD, and the header says why: 380 is held because the REFUSAL can block a rebuild; this is record-only, so there is no blocking behaviour to sequence. Carries every discipline 380 acquired over two council rounds — snapshot_agent, duplicate-active-row guard, already-applied guard, and a pre-flight assertion that the path exists and holds this action BEFORE any jsonb_set (create_missing:=true on a wrong path inserts a new branch and reports success, arming nothing while every reader says armed).
edits.sketch: BEGIN; snapshot_agent('page-rerender', ...); \echo BEFORE; DO block: assert exactly 1 live row, assert not already armed (IS TRUE); DO block: assert default_config #>> '{workflow,steps,rerender_sections,action}' = 'rerender_page_sections' else RAISE 'the workflow shape moved; re-derive the path'; UPDATE ... jsonb_set(default_config,'{workflow,steps,rerender_sections,config,record_dead_url_controls}','true',true); \echo AFTER; verify DO block (below); negative-control DO block (below); COMMIT; then a WATCH section with the demand control.

edits.rationale: Two checks that can each come out otherwise. VERIFY counts every rerender_page_sections step FLEET-WIDE (not scoped to page-rerender, so a second agent acquiring the step later fails this file) and demands all of them armed; aborts first if the count is ZERO, because a wrong traversal is otherwise indistinguishable from a clean pass; every comparison is IS TRUE / IS DISTINCT FROM, since a jsonb `<>` sits green for ever on an ABSENT key (NULL <> 'true' is NULL). NEGATIVE CONTROL asserts refuse_dead_url_controls is still true NOWHERE — this file must not arm the refusal, and if a later edit reaches for the wrong key then 380's owner-facing decision would be made silently here instead.
edits.sketch: verify: count(*) FILTER (action='rerender_page_sections') AS steps, count(*) FILTER (... AND (config->>'record_dead_url_controls')::boolean IS TRUE) AS armed over agent_definitions x LATERAL jsonb_path_query('strict $.**.steps') x jsonb_each; RAISE if steps=0 ('the traversal is wrong, so a green result here would mean nothing'); RAISE if armed<>steps. negative control: count of steps with refuse_dead_url_controls IS TRUE must be 0.

edits.rationale: Sets the key to explicit FALSE rather than removing it, for the reason 380's sidecar states: an absent key is indistinguishable from 'this seam was never wired here', so a deliberate disarm would read as an oversight. States what is kept (the Go half stays and is inert; DeadURLSlots and the per-section Error log still fire, so you keep the signal and lose only the durable item) and what is NOT undone (items already filed are not deleted — each names a real page and slot serving a dead control, and they are the only durable evidence this estate has for the ungated class).
edits.sketch: BEGIN; snapshot_agent; duplicate-row guard; UPDATE ... 'false'::jsonb; verify with IS NOT FALSE (absence = failure); COMMIT; then a report query listing every dead_url_control item already filed, so disarming is not mistaken for undoing.

plan.risks: Volume: one item per (page, slot, dead-field-set) on any re-render of a section rendering an empty src=/href=. Bounded by insertWorkItem's idx_swi_dedup-matched ON CONFLICT and its two-strike anti-churn label. ONE churn edge is stated rather than discovered: the item key embeds the SORTED dead-field list, so a PARTIAL repair changes the key and can mint a second item alongside a parked first one. Bounded, not zero; the close-out has to look for both. Between arming and the next chassis roll, the config report names record_dead_url_controls as unrecognised, because the declaration is Go. Cosmetic, warn-only (CheckConfig, not StrictConfig — verified at the deciding arm), and it is the stated cost of arming detection today rather than after a roll. Gated fields are NOT covered by this and cannot be: missingBareFields walks root-scope actions only, so a {{if .cardN_link_url}} guard keeps its field out of the report. For the gated class the only signal remains the 28 STRUCTURAL_KEY_CARRY_MISS findings, whose consumer is the NEXT submission (498/499). A gated field fails MORE quietly than an ungated one, which is the opposite of the intuition that gating is the safe pattern. A sustained zero after arming has TWO readings and the file says so: nothing is re-rendering a damaged section (plausible — the improvement loop and the discovery rotations are both paused on cost grounds, bugs_open/230), or the flag did not take. The verify block settles the second; the demand control settles the first (one 379-shape page_rerender at aao /index.html, whose five bare card*_image_url fields force missingBareFields non-empty). A traffic-free control cannot tell 'armed and quiet' from 'armed and blind'.
plan.non_scope: The refusal half (380_*_HOLD.sql) is NOT armed. It is gated on four measurable drain conditions after 498/499, and it stays a deliberate separate decision — the negative control in 497 exists to keep it that way. No new floor, guard or merge in save_page_sections (bugs_open/178's standing stop sign). This arms an existing render-path emit. No on_missing-driven render gate (RFC_009 option A, owner-DEAD 2026-08-03: ~90% of fields declare no on_missing). The 8 unguarded RenderTemplate call sites named in dead_url_guard.go's own header stay unguarded — the council already ruled making RenderTemplate the reporting form is RFC-shaped, and it is reserved as candidate RFC_042. Disjoint from bugs_open/312 and its held 477: 477 edits page-content-writer's select_sections field paths, this edits page-rerender's rerender_sections step config. Different agent, different step, different key. Nothing here requires 477, and applying 477 later neither needs nor undoes it.
